title: Regional traffic stitch and customer ops hotpatch for cross-region KV divergence
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a partial network churn in us-west-2 on 2026-03-09 we observed a class of client-visible errors for a subset of tenants using Dedicated capacity: requests routed across overlapping routing domains produced KV-cache divergence and sticky session mismatches. Symptoms included 502/504 spikes, inconsistent generation outputs for pinned model versions, and customer support escalations from three enterprise customers. Scope: Hosted and Dedicated fleets in us-west-2; Private/VPC customers not impacted. Impact: Intermittent but repeatable errors for ~0.7% of requests in the affected region over a 4-hour window, several high-severity customer tickets, and one escalation to SRE on-call for rollback coordination.
acceptance_criteria: Automated detection rule triggers within 90s of KV divergence state
Hotpatch rollout reduces error-rate on affected tenants to <0.05% within 15 minutes
Root-cause patch merged and smoke-tested on staging with latency regressions <3%
Customer-facing postmortem and remediation notes published within 3 business days
Runbook updated with clear 'traffic stitch' steps and rollback commands
steps: Detect: add short-lived telemetry metric 'kv_cohort_mismatch' and dashboard panel in grafana (done)
Mitigate (hotpatch): enable graceful-reshard mode and aggressive lease-renewal for leader leases in routing layer (rollout plan below)
Evacuate traffic: progressive 10% shift away from us-west-2 to warm standby region with tenant-prioritization (manual control via traffic-shift API)
Apply KV reconcile: issue synchronous KV snapshot-and-apply for mid-priority tenants, high-priority tenants use on-path repair
Validate: run deterministic prompt suite and sampling against pinned model versions for affected tenants
Rollback plan: revert lease-renewal toggle and resharding if error rate increases or latency degrades >10%
Customer comms: send interim status to affected accounts and create tailored remediation guidance
technical_notes: Root cause hypothesis: transient control-plane partition caused dual leaders for some KV shards while routing metadata caches accepted both leader addresses due to stale TTL handling
Immediate fix: enforce leader-lease monotonicity with a short, aggressive refresh window and add a fast-path that rejects conflicting leader writes until consensus achieved
Code changes: runtime/router: add 'force_renew_lease' flag and routing/cache: treat TTL < 5s as expired for route selection
Database impact: snapshot-and-apply uses existing KV repair job; ensure job concurrency limited to 8 shards/sec to avoid I/O spikes
Telemetry: emit 'kv_repair_duration_ms' and correlate with 'tenant_error_rate' for post-incident analysis
Tests: add unit tests for dual-leader detection and an integration test that simulates asymmetric lease renewal under network partitions
